final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Find common denominator
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite fraction parts as equivalent fractions before subtraction when denominators are not already aligned.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly finds an LCD or common denominator.
Tag when one or both fractions are converted to equivalent fractions to match denominators before subtracting.
Tag in mixed-number subtraction when only the fractional parts are being equalized.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no equivalent-fraction conversion is performed.
Do not tag steps that only subtract numerators or whole parts after setup is complete.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator unless the main purpose of the step is denominator alignment.

skills.name: Normalize subtraction form
skills.definition: Rewrite a mixed number or whole number into a subtraction-ready whole-and-fraction form, including normalizing improper mixed numbers and expressing whole numbers with a zero fractional part.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is converted to standard mixed-number form, such as 2 3/2 to 3 1/2.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0 over a denominator, such as 3 to 3 + 0/5.
Tag when a step explicitly prepares quantities so whole parts and fraction parts can be subtracted separately.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag equivalent-fraction conversion whose purpose is only to match denominators.
Do not tag borrowing or regrouping after subtraction reveals the fractional part is too small.
Do not tag final recombination of whole and fraction parts into the answer.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fraction parts with like denominators and/or subtract whole-number parts once the quantities are in compatible form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a shared denominator.
Tag when whole parts of mixed numbers are subtracted.
Tag when a solution performs separate whole-part and fraction-part subtraction after setup, even if the fractional result is initially zero or negative.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is finding a common denominator or rewriting numbers into subtraction-ready form.
Do not tag borrowing or regrouping steps used to repair a negative fractional difference.
Do not tag simplification or final answer formatting after subtraction.

skills.name: Regroup for subtraction
skills.definition: Borrow 1 from the whole-number part and convert it into fractional units when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly borrows 1 from the whole part.
Tag when 1 whole is rewritten as denominator over denominator and added to the fractional part.
Tag when regrouping is used after an initial negative fractional difference or anticipated insufficient fractional part.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag simple subtraction when no borrowing is needed.
Do not tag initial rewriting of a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator before subtraction.
Do not tag final combination of the answer after regrouping is complete.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce a fractional result to lowest terms or convert a zero fractional result to an integer or zero when appropriate.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is reduced by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor.
Tag when a result like 0 over a denominator is rewritten as 0.
Tag when a whole-number result is recognized because the fractional part simplifies to zero.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag subtraction steps that already produce an unsimplified or simplified result unless an explicit simplification is shown.
Do not tag mere recombination of whole and fraction parts if no reduction or zero-fraction cleanup occurs.
Do not tag normalization or regrouping steps.

skills.name: Compose final answer
skills.definition: Combine the computed whole-number and fractional parts and express the result in an acceptable final form such as a mixed number, fraction, integer, or zero.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when separate whole and fraction results are recombined into one final value.
Tag when a zero whole part is omitted to present a proper fraction.
Tag when a whole plus zero fraction is written as an integer or when the final answer is explicitly stated from previously computed parts.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag intermediate subtraction of whole or fraction parts before recombination.
Do not tag simplification alone unless the step also explicitly forms the final answer.
Do not tag initial rewrites used to prepare the subtraction.

decisions.details: Kept C01 as S01 (Find common denominator)
decisions.reasoning: This skill had 3/3 consensus and is clearly independent from subtraction itself. It explains denominator-alignment steps that occur in some items but not others, improving Q-matrix identifiability.

decisions.details: Merged the preparation aspects aligned under C02 into S02 (Normalize subtraction form), preserving both improper-mixed normalization and whole-to-whole-plus-zero-fraction rewriting
decisions.reasoning: Experts A and C already treated these as one broader preparation skill, while B split them. Across the item set, both are subtraction-readiness transformations rather than distinct arithmetic operations, and keeping them separate would create narrow, unevenly used skills with weaker independence.

decisions.details: Refined C02 name from 'Normalize mixed form' to S02 'Normalize subtraction form'
decisions.reasoning: The original canonical name underrepresented whole-number rewrites such as 3 to 3 + 0/5. The new name gives clearer boundaries and better matches the full set of included cases.

decisions.details: Kept C03 as S03 (Subtract aligned parts)
decisions.reasoning: This 3/3 consensus skill captures the core arithmetic subtraction once setup is complete. It remains distinct from denominator finding, normalization, regrouping, simplification, and final formatting.

decisions.details: Kept C04 as S04 (Regroup for subtraction)
decisions.reasoning: This skill had unanimous agreement and is diagnostically important because only a subset of mixed-number and whole-minus-fraction items require borrowing. It is clearly separable from both preparation and subtraction.

This post-subtraction operation appears in a distinct subset of items and is independently testable. It should remain separate from final answer composition because some items compose without simplifying, and some simplify before composing.

decisions.details: Kept C06 as S06 (Compose final answer)
decisions.reasoning: Although it often follows subtraction and simplification, it is a distinct representational step: recombining parts and presenting the answer in acceptable form. Keeping it separate preserves completeness and supports annotation of mixed-number assembly steps.

summary: The three expert codebooks showed near-complete agreement, so the final codebook preserves the shared six-skill structure. The only substantive consolidation issue was the preparation stage: Expert B split normalization and decomposition, while Experts A and C combined them. Following minimality, clarity, and identifiability principles, these were unified into one broader subtraction-readiness skill. The final codebook contains six distinct, diagnosable skills covering setup, subtraction, regrouping, simplification, and final expression.
